title: The part of AI decision-making that gets overlooked
author: MaleficentRisk3695
selftext:
I’ve noticed that people often focus on how quickly AI can process information, but not enough on what happens before a decision is made.

The rules used to interpret the information can matter just as much as the information itself. A system can process thousands of responses quickly and still produce inconsistent results if the underlying logic isn’t clear.

It’s an interesting reminder that automation doesn’t replace good decision-making. It mainly makes whatever process you already have run faster.

comments.author: ozgqr
comments.body: I’d model this as a decision pipeline rather than a single model output: data snapshot, feature interpretation, proposed action, risk gate, execution decision, and post-trade review. Which boundary do you think should own confidence—the model, the risk layer, or an evaluator that sees the full trajectory? Marx seems relevant to that separation of concerns.
